what: v4 model selection on data/built/fit/dev_fit.jsonl only (eval/protocol.json selection, eval/protocol_amendment_1.json tie-break). The fresh test was not scored or opened for this.

rule.text: The system TAG+H' with the higher macro-F1 on all 567 dev_fit rows; within 0.01 (|h - d3| <= 0.01) the incumbent d3 stays (amendment 1 selection.tie_break, since protocol.json's 'prefer the run without reasoning traces' cannot separate two runs that both have none).
rule.applied: h+H' 0.8132 - d3+H' 0.7706 = 0.0426 > 0.01: the higher macro-F1 wins, the tie-break does not apply (it would have picked d3 inside the margin)

why: higher macro-F1 by more than the tie margin (fit_eval_score.py dev)

dev_fit_all_rows.intervals: [point, 2.5th, 97.5th]; two-way bootstrap (postings, then rows), 2000 draws, seed 20261021

caveats: dev_fit was built by the same pipeline as h's training data (build_fit_train.py: hedged-wording twins, real venator postings, teasers, neutral_fill), so it favors h and is not evidence about generalization. Only the sealed fresh test speaks to that.
dev_fit gold is rules.label on each row's own card, so rules_full scores 1.0 here by construction and rules baselines are reported, not compared.

h's whole lead comes from the twins and teasers, the parts made by h's own training pipeline. On the 222 real venator postings h and d3 are level (macro-F1 0.7185 vs 0.7199) and both trail skills-free rules (0.9002) against this rules-made gold.

scoring.model_label: scripts/colab_eval.py: merged LoRA, bfloat16, batch 1 (--dtype bfloat16 --batch 1; RUN_CHOICE 'bfloat16 1' in both sessions), float32 label scores of Keep/Explore/Skip at the first answer token; fit_eval_score.py reads the label again (ties Skip, Explore, Keep) and checked every stored pred and row
scoring.prompts: data/built/fit/eval_inputs/h/dev_fit.jsonl for h, data/built/fit/eval_inputs/d3/dev_fit.jsonl for d3 (byte-identical, pinned in eval/fit_eval_hashes.json)

colab_sessions.matcher-d3-devfit: d3, L4, lost its connection before the merge (colab exec timed out); stopped, nothing scored
